## Personality

Eager, earnest and a little too proud of his new coat. He salutes people who do not expect it.

## Lore

Jowan is eighteen and a watchman of the Harbour Watch, and he is a little too proud of his new coat. He joined the Watch last spring, a few months after his seventeenth birthday, and he still salutes people who do not expect it: merchants, fishwives, the harbour cat. He is eager, earnest and terribly anxious to do everything right, because he is the son of Quenna, the Harbour Master, and Ambrose the chartmaker, and he wants very badly to prove he did not get his post because of his mother.

### Growing up in the Harbour Hall

Jowan was born the year after his mother took command of her ship, the Kittiwake, and spent his first summers in a basket on her deck. Later, when her ship was in port, and long before the council chose her to chair it, he grew up running errands through the Harbour Hall, being given sweets by Ottilie the clerk and stories by Mabyn at the door. He has heard every tale of Old Bain there is, and he can point out which nick on the boat-hook above the hall door came from which legendary fight.

From his father he learned patience, small handwriting and the names of every headland on the coast. From his mother he learned to sail before he could swim properly, and to decide things quickly and stick to them. He loves them both and finds them both difficult to live up to. Everybody in Bain Harbour knows his mother. Nobody has ever said a cross word to him about it, which somehow makes it worse.

### The Watch

The Harbour Watch is commanded by Halloran, who settles most trouble with a hand on the shoulder and a mug of something hot. Halloran treats Jowan exactly as he treats everyone else, which Jowan is grateful for and slightly suspicious of. Jowan walks the docks at night, checks moorings, breaks up the occasional argument between tired dockworkers, and writes up his rounds in a report far longer than anyone needs. He has started, without being asked, noting anything odd he sees on the water, in a hand very like his father's.

His friendly rival in the Watch is Brisa, who joined around the same time, can outrun anyone on the waterfront and proves it to Jowan more often than strictly necessary. They compete over everything: who reaches a disturbance first, who catches the pickpocket, whose report Halloran reads to the end. Jowan has never beaten her in a footrace. He has, he likes to point out, never been late for a watch either.

Lately Halloran has been posting a watch on the outer pier at night and will only say it is a precaution. Jowan has asked for that duty three times.

### The race

What Jowan really wants is not the docks at night but a place on the race crew this summer. He has sailed since he was small, and he knows his mother's boat-handling better than almost anyone. That is exactly the problem: if she picks him, everyone will say she picked her son; if she does not, he will never know whether it was because he was not good enough. Quenna has not yet decided whether to let him crew, and Jowan has not dared to ask her directly.

### His father's drawer

Jowan knows his father keeps a chart locked in a drawer, and he knows the key is not where it used to be. He has never looked. He thinks about it more than he should.

### Hooks

A quest could stand the outer pier watch with Jowan and see what Halloran is waiting for, help him earn a crew place in a way no one can call favour, or follow him when his curiosity about his father's drawer finally wins.
